86.h: 82 - Ubayy ibn Kaʿb ibn Qays ibn ʿUbayd al-Anṣārī * (ع)
86.t:
ibn Zayd ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr ibn Mālik ibn al-Najjār. ⟦1:389⟧
The master of the reciters (القارئ), Abū Mundhir al-Anṣārī, al-Najjārī, al-Madanī, the Qurʾān reciter (المقرئ), the Badrī (البدري).
He is also known by the patronymic (الكنية): Abū al-Ṭufayl.
He was present at al-ʿAqabah and at Badr, collected the Qurʾān during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, recited it to the Prophet (peace be upon him), and memorised from him blessed knowledge; and he was a head in knowledge and practice (may Allah be pleased with him).
Narrating from him: بنوه؛ محمد، والطفيل، وعبد الله، وأنس بن مالك، وابن عباس، وسويد بن غفلة، وزر بن حبيش، وأبو العالية الرياحي (1) ، وأبو عثمان النهدي، وسليمان بن صرد، وسهل بن سعد، وأبو إدريس الخولاني، وعبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل، وعبد الرحمن بن أبزى، وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، وعبيد بن عمير، وعتي (2) السعدي، وابن الحوتكية، وسعيد بن المسيب، وكأنه مرسل، وآخرون.
From ʿĪsā ibn Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, who said:
Ubayy was a stocky man – meaning of medium build – neither tall nor short.
From Ibn ʿAbbās ibn Sahl, who said:
Ubayy was white of head (3) and beard.
Anas said:
The Prophet ﷺ said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: (Allah has commanded me to recite the Qurʾān to you).
In another wording: (He has commanded me to teach you the recitation of the Qurʾān).
He said: Allah named me to you?
He said: (Yes).
He said: And I was mentioned before the Lord of the Worlds?
He said: (Yes).
And his eyes shed tears (4). ⟦1:390⟧
And when the Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy: (Which verse in the Qurʾān is the greatest?).
Ubayy said: “Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence” [al-Baqarah (1) : 255].
The Prophet ﷺ struck him on his chest and said: (May knowledge be a delight to you, Abū al-Mundhir).
Anas ibn Mālik said: Four men collected the Qurʾān in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, all of them from the Anṣār: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, Zayd ibn Thābit, and Abū Zayd, one of my paternal uncles (2).
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
Ubayy said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: I received the Qurʾān from the one who received it from Gabriel (peace be upon him) while it was fresh (3).
Ibn ʿAbbās said:
ʿUmar said: The best judge among us is ʿAlī, and the best reciter among us is Ubayy, yet we leave aside some of Ubayy's recitation traditions (القراءات).
Yet he says: I will not leave anything I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah the Exalted has said: “Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it” [al-Baqarah: 106] (4). ⟦1:391⟧
وروى: أبو قلابة، عن أنس، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The best reciter of my community is Ubayy (1)).
From Abū Saʿīd, who said:
Ubayy said: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ! What is the reward for fever?
He said: (Good deeds keep flowing to the one who has it).
He said: O Allah, I ask You for a fever that does not prevent me from going out in Your path.
After that Ubayy was never touched without fever being upon him (2).
I say: The constant fever upon him altered his temper slightly, and that is why Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh says: There was a harshness in Ubayy.
Abū Naḍrah al-ʿAbdī said:
A man from among us called Jābir, or Juwaybir, said:
I went to ʿUmar with a request, and beside him was a man with white clothes and white hair, who said:
This world holds our sufficiency and our provision for the Hereafter, and in it are our deeds for which we will be recompensed in the Hereafter.
I said: Who is this, O Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين)?
He said: This is the master of the Muslims, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (3).
قال مغيرة بن مسلم: عن الربيع، عن أنس، عن أبي العالية، قال:
A man said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: Advise me.
He said: Take the Book of Allah as your leader, and be content with it as judge and arbiter, ⟦1:392⟧ for it is what your Messenger left behind among you: an intercessor who is obeyed, and a witness who is not suspected; in it is mention of you and of those before you, judgement on what is between you, news of you, and news of what comes after you (1).
الثوري، وأبو جعفر الرازي - واللفظ له -: عن الربيع بن أنس، عن أبي العالية، عن أبي: “Say: He is the One Able to send upon you a punishment from above you” (Qurʾān 6:65), he said:
They are four, all of them punishment, and all of them certain to occur; two have passed, 25 years after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: they were confounded into factions, and some of them tasted the violence of others; and two remain, certain to occur: being swallowed by the earth, and stoning (2).
أخبرنا إسحاق الأسدي، أنبأنا يوسف الحافظ، أنبأنا أحمد بن محمد، أنبأنا أبو علي المقرئ، أنبأنا أبو نعيم، حدثنا محمد بن إسحاق بن أيوب، حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعدان، حدثنا بكر بن بكار، حدثنا عبد الحميد بن جعفر، حدثني أبي، عن سليمان بن يسار، عن عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل، قال:
I was standing with Ubayy ibn Kaʿb in the shade of the fortress of Ḥassān, where the market is the fruit market today.
Ubayy said: Do you not see the people, their necks turned every way in pursuit of this world?
I said: Indeed.
He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (Soon the Euphrates will uncover a mountain of gold, and when the people hear of it they will march toward it, and those who are by it will say: If we let the people take from it, they will leave nothing of it; so the people will fight (3), and of every 100, 99 will be killed (4)). ⟦1:393⟧
Muslim recorded it by way of ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd.
He has another chain of transmission (الإسناد), namely: الزبيدي، عن الزهري، عن إسحاق مولى المغيرة، عن أبي (1) .
أبو صالح الكاتب: حدثنا موسى بن علي، عن أبيه:
That ʿUmar delivered a sermon at al-Jābiyah and said:
Whoever wants to ask about the Qurʾān, let him come to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb; whoever wants to ask about the shares of inheritance, let him come to Zayd; whoever wants to ask about jurisprudence (الفقه), let him come to Muʿādh; and whoever wants to ask about wealth, let him come to me, for Allah has made me a treasurer and a distributor (2).
al-Wāqidī also narrated it from Mūsā.
أبو بكر بن عياش: عن عاصم، عن زر، قال:
I came to Medina and went to Ubayy, and said:
May Allah have mercy on you! Lower your wing for me – and he was a man with a harshness in him –.
I asked him about Laylat al-Qadr, and he said: The night of the twenty-seventh (3).
سفيان الثوري: عن أسلم المنقري، عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن بن أبزى، عن أبيه، قال:
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: (I have been commanded to recite the Qurʾān to you).
I said: O Messenger of Allah! And I was named to you?
He said: (Yes).
I said to Ubayy: Were you glad of that?
He said: And what would stop me, when He the Exalted says: “Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, in that let them rejoice” [Yūnus: 58] (4). ⟦1:394⟧
In corroboration (المتابعة) of him: الأجلح، عن عبد الله، عن أبيه.
محمد بن عيسى بن الطباع: حدثنا معاذ بن محمد بن محمد بن أبي بن كعب، عن أبيه، عن جده، عن أبي:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (O Abū al-Mundhir! I have been commanded to present the Qurʾān to you).
I said: In Allah I have believed, at your hand I have embraced Islam, and from you I have learned.
He repeated the words, and I said: O Messenger of Allah! And was I mentioned there?
He said: (Yes, by your name and your lineage, in the Highest Assembly).
I said: Then recite, O Messenger of Allah (1).
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī narrated it from Ibn al-Ṭabbāʿ, and said:
Muʿādh ibn Muḥammad ibn Muʿādh ibn Ubayy narrated to us.
سفيان: عن الأعمش، عن أبي وائل، عن مسروق:
From ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, raised (المرفوع): (Learn the recitation of the Qurʾān from four: from Ibn Masʿūd, Ubayy, Muʿādh, and Sālim the client (المولى) of Abū Ḥudhayfah (2)).
Abū Dāwūd recorded, from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar:
That the Prophet ﷺ performed a prayer and became confused in it, and when he finished, he said to Ubayy: (Did you pray with us?).
He said: Yes.
He said: (Then what prevented you?) (3). ⟦1:395⟧
شعبة: عن أبي جمرة (1) ، حدثنا إياس بن قتادة، عن قيس بن عباد، قال:
I came to Medina to meet the companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, and there was no man among them I would rather meet than Ubayy. The prayer was called, and he came out, and I stood in the first row.
Then a man came and looked into the faces of the people, and he recognised them all except me, so he moved me aside and stood in my place, and I could not keep my mind on my prayer.
When he had prayed, he said: My son! May Allah not grieve you; I did not do what I did out of ignorance, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: (Be in the row that is next to me).
And I looked into the faces of the people and recognised them all except you. And it was Ubayy (may Allah be pleased with him) (2).
الدارمي (3) : حدثنا يحيى بن حسان، حدثنا عكرمة بن إبراهيم، أخبرنا يزيد بن شداد، حدثني معاوية بن قرة، حدثني عتبة بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص، حدثني أبي، عن جدي، قال:
I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a day of ʿĪd, and he said: (Call for me the master of the Anṣār?).
So they called Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
He said: (O Ubayy! Go to Baqīʿ al-Muṣallā and order it to be swept), and the rest of the hadith (4). ⟦1:396⟧
الوليد بن مسلم: حدثنا عبد الله بن العلاء، عن عطية بن قيس، عن أبي إدريس الخولاني:
That Abū al-Dardāʾ (1) rode to Medina with a group of the people of Damascus, and one day they recited to ʿUmar: “When those who disbelieved put into their hearts the fury, the fury of the Jāhiliyyah (الجاهلية)” [al-Fatḥ: 26], and had you felt fury as they felt fury, the Sacred Mosque would have been corrupted.
ʿUmar said: Who taught you to recite this?
They said: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
So he summoned him, and when he came (2), he said: Recite.
So they recited it likewise.
Ubayy said: By Allah, O ʿUmar, you know that I used to be present while they were absent, and I was admitted close while they were kept out, and this was done for me and that was done for me; and by Allah, if you wish, I shall keep to my house, narrate nothing, and teach no one to recite until I die.
ʿUmar said: O Allah, forgiveness! We know that Allah has placed knowledge with you, so teach the people what you know (3).
ابن عيينة: عن عمرو، عن بجالة - أو غيره - قال:
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb passed by a boy reading from a copy of the Qurʾān: “The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers” [al-Aḥzāb: 61] and he is a father to them.
He said: Boy! Scratch it out.
He said: This is Ubayy's copy of the Qurʾān.
So he went to him and asked him, and he said: The Qurʾān used to occupy me, while clapping hands on deals in the markets occupied you (4).
عوف: عن الحسن، حدثني عتي بن ضمرة، قال:
I saw the people of Medina ⟦1:397⟧ surging in their streets.
I said: What is the matter with these people?
One of them said: Are you not from the people of this town?
I said: No.
He said: The master of the Muslims, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, has died today (1).
أيوب: عن أبي قلابة، عن أبي المهلب، عن أبي، قال:
We complete it in eight nights – meaning the Qurʾān (2) –.
Sallām ibn Miskīn: ʿImrān ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: Why do you not appoint me to office?
He said: I dislike that your religion should be sullied (3).
الأعمش: عن حبيب بن أبي (4) ثابت، عن سعيد (5) بن جبير، عن ابن عباس:
ʿUmar said: Come out with us to the land of our people.
I was at the rear of the people with Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and a cloud rose up, and he said: O Allah, avert its harm from us.
He said: Then we caught up with them, and their saddles had become wet.
ʿUmar said: Did what struck us not strike you?
I said: Abū al-Mundhir said: O Allah, avert its harm from us.
He said: Why then did you not pray for us along with yourselves (6).
Maʿmar said: Most of the knowledge of Ibn ʿAbbās came from three: ʿUmar, ʿAlī and Ubayy.
Masrūq said: I asked Ubayy about something, and he said: Has it happened yet?
I said: No. He said: ⟦1:398⟧
Then spare us until it happens; when it happens, we will exert independent legal reasoning (الاجتهاد) and give you our personal opinion (الرأي).
الجريري: عن أبي نضرة، قال:
A man from among us, called Jābir or Juwaybir, said:
I came to ʿUmar, and I had been given eloquence, so I began speaking about this world and belittled it until I left it worth nothing; and beside him was a man white of head, beard and clothes.
He said: All your speech is reasonable, except your attack on this world. Do you know what this world is? In it is our sufficiency -or he said: our provision- for the Hereafter, and in it are our deeds for which we will be recompensed.
I said: Who is this, O Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين)?
He said: This is the master of the Muslims, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (1).
أصرم بن حوشب: عن أبي جعفر الرازي، عن الربيع بن أنس، عن أبي العالية، قال:
Ubayy was a man of worship, and when the people came to need him, he left off worship and sat for the people (2).
عوف: عن الحسن، عن عتي بن ضمرة:
I said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: What is the matter with you, O companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ! We come to you from far away, hoping for good from you, and you treat us lightly?
He said: By Allah, if I live until this Friday, I shall say a word without caring whether you spare me or kill me.
When Friday came, I went out, and there were the people of Medina surging in its streets.
I said: What is the news?
They said: The master of the Muslims, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, has died (3).
I have mentioned the reports of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb in (Ṭabaqāt al-Qurrāʾ), and that Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-ʿĀliyah and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Sāʾib recited to him, and that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAyyāsh al-Makhzūmī recited ⟦1:399⟧ to him as well; and ʿUmar used to revere Ubayy, behave courteously toward him, and take disputes to him for judgement.
Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Wāqidī said: Hadiths indicate that Ubayy ibn Kaʿb died during the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar, and I saw his family and others saying:
He died in the year 22 at Medina, and that ʿUmar said: Today the master of the Muslims has died.
He said: We have heard someone say: He died during the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUthmān, in the year 30.
He said: That is the most firmly established of the statements in our view, because ʿUthmān ordered him to collect the Qurʾān.
Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: حدثنا عارم، حدثنا حماد، عن أيوب، عن ابن سيرين:
That ʿUthmān gathered 12 men of Quraysh and the Anṣār, among them Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Zayd ibn Thābit, for the compilation of the Qurʾān (1).
I say: This is a strong chain of transmission (الإسناد), but it is mursal (مرسل); and I do not think that ʿUthmān assigned Ubayy to the muṣḥaf, for had that been so it would have become well known, and the mention would have been of Ubayy, not of Zayd. What is apparent is that Ubayy died in the time of ʿUmar, so much so that al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī and others mentioned his death in the year 19.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr, Abū ʿUbayd and Abū ʿUmar al-Ḍarīr said:
He died in the year 22, and the mind inclines more to this.
As for Khalīfah ibn Khayyāṭ and Abū Ḥafṣ al-Fallās, they said:
He died during the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUthmān.
Khalīfah said on one occasion: He died in the year 32.
In (the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd):
يونس بن عبيد: عن الحسن:
That ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb gathered the people behind Ubayy ibn Kaʿb for the night prayer of Ramaḍān, and he used to pray 20 ⟦1:400⟧ rakʿahs with them (1).
Ubayy once picked up a purse containing 100 dinars; he announced it for a year and then took possession of it, and that is in (the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين)). ⟦1:401⟧
Ibn ʿAbbās narrated from him the story of Mūsā and al-Khiḍr, and that is in (the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين) (1)) too.
Ubayy has in the Six Books (الكتب الستة): 60-odd hadiths.
The hadith master (الحافظ) Abū Muḥammad al-Nūnī informed me of his lineage, and said:
Mālik ibn al-Najjār: he is the brother of ʿAdī, Dīnār and Māzin.
And the name of al-Najjār, their father: Taym Allāh (2) ibn Thaʿlabah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-Khazraj.
He said: And Ubayy ibn Kaʿb is the son of the paternal aunt of Abū Ṭalḥah al-Anṣārī.
Ubayy was slight, short, and white of head and beard.
al-Wāqidī said: I saw his family and more than one person saying:
He died in the year 22 at Medina.
And I heard someone say: He died during the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUthmān, in the year 30, and that is the most firmly established of the statements in our view.
He said: Because ʿUthmān ordered him to collect the Qurʾān.
روى: حماد بن زيد، عن أيوب وهشام، عن ابن سيرين:
That ʿUthmān gathered 12 men of Quraysh and the Anṣār, among them: Ubayy and Zayd ibn Thābit, for the compilation of the Qurʾān (3).
He has with Baqī ibn Makhlad: 164 hadiths, of which in al-Bukhārī and Muslim: 3 hadiths.
al-Bukhārī alone has 3, and Muslim alone 7. ⟦1:402⟧
